column1: # Custom property-id registry - single authority for FORK-allocated property enum ids.
# Reserve an id here BEFORE the code that uses it lands. Two branches claiming the same id then
# collide as a git conflict in this file instead of as a silent post-merge duplicate.
# Motivating case: PropertyInt 9032 was claimed twice on the same day (PR #222 vs
# feature/equipment-mods). CI's duplicate-id test catches that only AFTER both sides merge.
# Flow: Docs/Runbook.md, "Reserving a custom property id".
#   status=reserved -> claimed, the code is not on master yet, so the enum member need not exist.
#                      If it DOES exist it must still name-match, so a reserved row needs no edit
#                      when its branch lands - only a flip to active once it is on master.
#   status=active   -> the enum member exists on master and MUST name-match this row exactly.
# A range row (id_or_range = "start-end") reserves a whole block and carries a block LABEL, not an
# enum name. It does not satisfy the per-id requirement: allocating an id inside a reserved block
# means splitting a single-id row out of it.
# Guarded bands: every enum member whose value falls inside a band below must have a row here with
# the exact same name. Enforced by Source/ACE.Server.Tests/PropertyRegistryTests.cs.
# Deliberately OUTSIDE the guarded bands, because these ids are not this fork's to allocate:
#   - PCAP recorder ids from upstream ACEmulator's packet-capture tooling:
#   - Upstream ACEmulator's own custom properties, which arrive here via upstream merges:
# Each fork band therefore starts one id past the last upstream allocation in that enum. An
# upstream merge that lands a NEW member inside a fork band fails the registry test on purpose:
# that is a genuine collision needing a decision, not a false alarm.
# Machine-readable band declarations - the test reads these lines, so keep them and the prose above
# enum_file is the enum name; the file is Source/ACE.Entity/Enum/Properties/<enum_file>.cs.
# Rows are tab-separated and sorted by enum_file (ordinal), then by id / range start.

World Events boss confinement: on a creature, omit MovementParamFlags.Sticky in Creature.GetMovementParameters (FailWalk, UseFinalHeading and MoveAway are unchanged). Mule Form Token: marks an item as a mule form token. per-character chat toggle set by the player command /summondamage on|off (default off, i.e. absent). When true the pet owner - and only the owner - gets one chat line per hit their own summoned pet lands. Read in Pet.NotifyOwnerOfDamage, called from the four routes a pet's damage takes to a creature's health: Creature.TakeDamage (melee via Monster_Melee, missile via ProjectileCollisionHelper), SpellProjectile.DamageTarget (spell projectiles), WorldObject_Magic.HandleCastSpell_Boost's Health case (Harm) and HandleCastSpell_Transfer's Health case (Drain Health). On a creature: this creature's death may CREATE the killer's (and eligible fellows') kill-task quest registry row instead of only crediting a row they already hold, exactly like the Bluespire ladder's own bootstrap (BluespireLadderRewards.ShouldBootstrapClearRow) but decided per-creature instead of by a fixed six-name table. SLOT-1 ONLY: applies only to the primary KillQuest slot (PropertyString 45) - KillQuest2/KillQuest3 stay HasQuest-gated regardless of this property, via Creature.ShouldBypassHasQuestGate's isPrimarySlot parameter. Absent or false is the default - every kill task in the game keeps its historic HasQuest gate. Set true on the Menhir Drummer (1003262), so the kill counts for a player (and fellows) who has not yet accepted Kanokeh's charge - Kanokeh arms BluespireMenhirDrummer with SetQuestCompletions amount 0 at charge ACCEPTANCE (Content/sql/weenies/1003202 Hea Kanokeh the Drum-Keeper.sql:30-31,460-466), which would otherwise be the only way the row is ever created. That arm is guarded against wiping a pre-kill's row by #1291. Fixed 2026-09-25 after 1003262's KillQuest2 briefly carried an unrelated quest (AunTumerokBountyCount) and inherited the bypass for it - see (now-deleted, 2026-09-26) Content/sql/patches/marae_lassel_killquest_auntumerok.sql; the fix itself (never tagging 1003262) is unchanged by that deletion.

ML Treasure Hunt: marks a treasure map instance as created by the admin /testtreasuremap command. Two effects: FinishDig reports MlDigsiteManager.TryStart's refusal reason to the digger in chat (a non-test map stays silent, as today), and MlRelariaSpawner.TrySpawn skips the IsBossSite catalogue check for this map's dig, since a test map's site was stamped at the admin's own position rather than rolled from the catalogue. Absent means an ordinary map, dropped or rerolled normally.

THE hook gate; the anchor also carries PG ids int 9029/9031 and float 9004, but the PG portal carries 9031 too, so the hook never keys on those alone

Refire/give-target stations refuse a locked item outright. See ACE.Server.Entity.TinkerLock (mechanism is generic, not wcid-specific). Read from the item's OWN biota only - no weenie fallback, no migration, no shard write. Stamped on the 8 Bluespire quest weapons (1005450-1005457, allow-list = the cook_book rows for the 4 Ward-Stones + 2 Thirst-Stones) ONLY - the 3 Siraluun crests (1005480-1005482) do NOT carry this property (owner ruling, 2026-09-27, reversing an earlier draft) and tinker normally. Next free id in the PropertyBool fork band (9011-9999) above the prior high-water 9067 (WaveEncounterAnchor).

Placement opt-in: a Stuck object carrying this spawns at EXACTLY its authored position instead of being pushed out of baked geometry by the spawn placement insert (walls, and the dat's baked static props, which Ethereal does not bypass). Cached at WorldObject.InitPhysicsObj onto PhysicsObj.ExactPlacement (via WorldObject.ExactPlacementStatic, which also requires Stuck) and honoured once, on enter_world, by PhysicsObj.ForceIntoCellExact. Honoured only on a Stuck non-creature, or on a Creature that is Stuck AND AiImmobile (52) AND NpcLooksLikeObject (83) (WorldObject.ExactPlacementRefusal); anything else is refused with a one-time warning per wcid. Absent is the unchanged retail path. First users: the Marketplace Salvage Forge (1002652) and Arcane Alignment Table (1002751), each set into a baked table. 9068 was skipped because origin/master holds it (TinkerLocked)

Per-character preference: run the full server-side physics simulation (Player.FastTick) for this player. ABSENT means follow the server property fast_tick_all_players (default false); set true/false by the player via /fasttick on|off, and /fasttick default removes it. An explicit true or false overrides the server property in either direction. PK/PKLite players are always fast tick regardless (Player.FastTick calls FastTickPolicy.Resolve(IsPKType, FastTickOptIn, FastTickPolicy.AllPlayers)). Read via Player.FastTickOptIn through FastTickPolicy.Resolve. The /fasttick command refuses a change that would alter the effective mode unless the player is idle (Player.FastTickChangeBlocker).

PvP Template Facets (Docs/Pvp/TEMPLATES.md): on an item, marks it as part of an issued template kit (cloned with a fresh guid, Attuned, Bonded, Value 0). Issued items are economy-locked always, destroyed on every template exit, and destroyed by the login sweep keyed on this mark ALONE, never on whether a restore record exists. Tested only through PvpTemplate.IsIssued, which recurses into containers
